fields.meta_description: Build an onboarding survey that checks in at day 30, 60 and 90, alerts IT to first-day gaps, and tracks each hiring cohort. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Onboarding Survey Timed to Each New Start
fields.hero_description: Create an onboarding survey timed to each hire's start date that flags first-day gaps and stores each answer in your own database.
fields.features_heading: What an Onboarding Survey Needs to Do
fields.features_subheading: An onboarding survey asks new hires, at set points in their first months, whether they have what they need to do the job.
fields.feature_1:
Check-ins keyed to the start date

Sends each check-in on a day you choose, counted from the hire date in your HR records and not from the calendar. Someone who starts mid-month gets day 30 on their own day 30.
fields.feature_2:
One question repeated every round

Asks the same core question at every checkpoint, such as whether the role is clear yet. A score that falls between day 30 and day 60 shows up next to that hire's name in the report.
fields.feature_3:
Results by team and manager

Reports answers by department and start month. Groups under a minimum you set stay hidden, and a team that hired two people this quarter never exposes either person's replies.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts for gaps that need a fix

Flags any hire who answers no to a question you mark urgent, like a missing login or no assigned buddy. Whoever owns that item gets an email or a Slack message the same day.
fields.feature_5:
Hire details pulled from HR

Reads each hire's manager and department from your HR system through its API. The survey never has to ask a new hire who they report to, and every answer splits by team.
fields.feature_6:
The whole survey app is yours

Exports the survey, its send schedule, the alert rules, and the response database to GitHub on paid plans. Run it on your own servers or keep changing it by prompting in Emergent.

fields.tab_content_1:
Three check-ins timed to one start date

Counted from the start date in BambooHR, each new hire hears from HR on day 30, day 60 and day 90. Every round repeats one question about role clarity. Priya Nair, a new account executive at Fernway, got her eight-question check-in for day 60 this morning, and her answers will sit beside the ones from day 30.
fields.tab_content_2:
A missing login reaches IT on day one

At 5 p.m. on the first day, each hire answers five yes-or-no questions on their phone, starting with the laptop and the logins. A no on either sends Sam Ortiz, the IT lead, a direct message naming the hire, and the missing item. Today it was Grace Liu, who could not open Salesforce.
fields.tab_content_3:
Since May, more hires know who to ask

Each month's new hires form a cohort, and every cohort is asked at day 30 whether they know who to ask for help. Fernway started pairing hires with a buddy in May. In the four months before, 35 of 60 hires said yes. In June, 20 of 24 did, and HR can show leadership the month the line turned.
fields.tab_content_4:
Setup calls for workspaces of 50 or more

Right after signup, a software product asks three questions on one screen: role, seat count, and the first task the user wants done. The answers pick the setup checklist. Workspaces with 50 or more seats are also offered a call with Lena Park, the onboarding lead. Each request lands in HubSpot.

fields.howto_title: How to Run an Onboarding Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan an onboarding survey around a hire's first 90 days, route urgent answers to an owner, and build it in Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write a short set for each
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Name an owner for urgent answers
fields.howto_step_1_des: Check in on the first day, then every 30 days until day 90. Give each checkpoint its own job: day one checks logistics, day 30 checks clarity and day 90 checks whether the hire plans to stay. Skip weekly surveys in the first month, when a new hire already has plenty to read.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Keep each round to eight questions or fewer. Use a five-point agreement scale for most of them, one yes-or-no gate for anything urgent, and one open box. Repeat a single core question in every round, because a trend needs the same wording each time.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A confidential survey shows HR who answered, and an anonymous one stores no identity at all. Confidential lets HR follow up with one person about a missing login. Say which kind it is on the first screen, in plain words, before question one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the two or three answers that need action within a day, like a laptop that never arrived. Give each one a single owner, such as the IT lead or the hiring manager. Everything else waits for the monthly review.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the brief the way you would explain it to a new HR coordinator, including who sees what and who gets alerted. Emergent builds the questions, the timed sends, a response database, and a dashboard. Changing a question later takes one more message.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect BambooHR or any HR system with an API. Start dates and managers then come from records HR already keeps. New hires join the schedule from that record, and nobody has to upload a spreadsheet of names each month.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once a month, set the newest cohort beside the ones before it on the repeated question. Look for the one team or step where answers drop. Fix that step, then check whether the next cohort answers differently.

plan.angle: The top 10 is question lists (Formbricks, Culture Amp, SurveyMonkey, Qualtrics, HiBob, Workleap, 360Learning), a SHRM form, Cornell's new-hire survey program and one product-onboarding post from Userpilot. None of them shows when each question should go out or what happens to an answer. This page answers the PAA questions on the 5 C's, the 30-60-90 rule and onboarding levels, then shows the survey running: timed off the start date, a first-day check that reaches IT the same evening, cohort trends that test an onboarding change, and a signup survey for software teams.
tab_stories: A new account executive at Fernway gets a short check-in on day 30, 60 and 90 counted from her BambooHR start date, and her day-60 survey goes out this morning with the same role-clarity question she answered at day 30.

At the end of the first day every hire answers five yes-or-no questions on a phone, and anyone who could not log in to a tool triggers a direct message to the IT lead naming the hire and the missing account.
Comparing monthly hiring cohorts shows that after a buddy program started in May, the share of hires who know who to ask for help at day 30 rose from 58% to 83%.

A software product asks new signups three questions on the first screen, and a workspace of 50 or more seats is offered a setup call with a named onboarding specialist while smaller teams get a self-serve checklist.

scope.evidence: H1 "Build an Onboarding Survey Timed to Each New Start"; hero "Create an onboarding survey timed to each hire's start date that flags first-day gaps and stores each answer in your own database." (D1 ok); how-to description one sentence (D2 ok).

intent.evidence: Top 10 is question lists and templates; page gives a definition, good questions by checkpoint, what to include, 30-60-90 timing, manager questions, questions to avoid, and a 7-step how-to.

specificity.evidence: "counted from the hire date in your HR records", "a missing login or no assigned buddy", "35 of 60 hires", employee table variant with competitors that rank (Culture Amp, Qualtrics, SurveyMonkey).

openers.evidence: "Counted from the start date in BambooHR", "At 5 p.m. on the first day", "Each month's new hires form a cohort", "Right after signup"; feature bodies open on verbs.

craft.evidence: "Keep each round to eight questions or fewer." "Everything else waits for the monthly review." QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean; one stray comma kept as a note.

voice.evidence: Concrete details (Grace Liu "could not open Salesforce", day-60 check-in "this morning", "Salesforce says my account is not set up."); no AI-tell vocabulary.

truth.evidence: faq item 7: "since a new hire has had one paycheck at most" is false for the day-60 and day-90 rounds the page itself recommends. Image numbers agree: 35/60 = 58%, 20/24 = 83%, up 25 points.

distinct.evidence: Owns the first 90 days (checkpoints, first-day check, cohorts, product signups); links exit-survey and employee-engagement-survey. Template overlap with exit-survey kept as a note.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, answer-first; hub link in item 2; links to exit-survey and employee-engagement-survey; F9 lines in items 8 and 9; PAA gate 10/10.

images.evidence: Priya Nair day 60 sent, 8 questions from Northwind HR; phone with five yes/no, Logins No, DM to Sam Ortiz about Grace Liu; cohort 58 to 83; Globex 120 seats gets a setup call with Lena Park, HubSpot log. One hero each, readable.
